header.html: exam strategy and review of every skill
the official AI-901 study guide, skills measured as of April 15, 2026

toc.title: Pairs the exam likes to confuse

html:
1Time and format

The duration and the number of questions are not given on the pages this course was built from, so check the exam page and divide the time by the number of questions. [Verify live]

Step Rule
First pass Answer what you know quickly; mark the rest
Second pass Return to marked questions
Last minutes No question left blank

Note

. Some exams contain sections that cannot be reviewed after you move on. Read the on-screen instructions before each section.

2The routine for every question

  1. Read the last sentence first.
  2. Find the key need: text, speech, image, document, agent, safety, cost, settings.
  3. Name the workload or the Foundry feature and drop options from other areas.
  4. Pick the most specific match.
  5. For a code question, read: client, credential, call, input, output.
  6. Mark and move on if two options remain after a minute.

3Checklists

Identify AI concepts and capabilities (40–45%)

  • The six principles and a clue for each: fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency, accountability
  • Tokens, transformer and attention, embeddings, context window, no memory between calls, hallucinations, grounding
  • Model kinds: LLM, SLM, reasoning, multimodal, image generation, embedding
  • Deployment: Global Standard, Data Zone, provisioned, batch; the catalog's two categories
  • Parameters: temperature (low focused, high varied), top_p, max tokens; reasoning models differ
  • The six workloads: generative, agentic, text analysis, speech, vision, information extraction
  • Text techniques: key phrases, entities, sentiment, summarization (extractive vs abstractive), language detection, PII
  • Speech: recognition (real-time, fast, batch), synthesis (neural, custom voice, SSML), translation
  • Vision: caption, tags, object detection, Read (OCR), people; image generation creates images
  • Extraction: documents, images, audio, video; extract, classify, generate; confidence and grounding

Implement AI solutions by using Microsoft Foundry (55–60%)

  • System vs user prompt; few-shot; ground with source text; "I don't know" rule
  • Foundry resource, project, endpoint; portal Build → Catalog → Deploy; playground, compare mode
  • SDK chat client: AIProjectClient, DefaultAzureCredential, get_openai_client, responses.create(model, input), output_text
  • Agent = model + instructions + tools; prompt, voice and hosted agents; tools (file search, code interpreter, web search, function calling, MCP); conversation keeps history
  • Text app: TextAnalyticsClient, analyze_sentiment; speech app: SpeechConfig, AudioConfig, SpeechRecognizer
  • Multimodal: user content list with text and image parts; images.generate, base64 result
  • Content Understanding: analyzers (prebuilt, custom), begin_analyze, poller.result()

4Pairs the exam likes to confuse

Pair Tell them apart
System vs user prompt developer rules vs the person's question
Generative vs agentic AI creates content vs uses tools to act toward a goal
Text analysis vs generative AI facts about existing text vs new text
Speech recognition vs synthesis audio to text vs text to audio
Analyze an image vs generate an image understand a picture vs create a picture
Extractive vs abstractive summary picks sentences vs writes new ones
Extract vs classify vs generate value as written vs a category vs a written value
Prebuilt vs custom analyzer common scenarios vs your own fields
Standard vs provisioned vs batch pay per token vs reserved capacity vs discounted asynchronous
Temperature vs max tokens randomness vs length
Fairness vs inclusiveness equal treatment of groups vs usable by everyone
Transparency vs accountability understandable vs someone responsible
Resource vs project the Azure container vs your workspace
Real-time vs batch transcription streaming vs many files later

5Common traps

  • "AI-900 materials are fine." AI-900 was retired on June 30, 2026.
  • "The model remembers earlier calls." It has no memory; the app resends messages (or uses a conversation).
  • "Higher temperature means more accurate." It means more varied.
  • "Reasoning models accept temperature." They do not.
  • "Tokens are words." Tokens can be sub-words.
  • "Images go in the system prompt." An image goes in the user message as an image part.
  • "A confidence score of 1 is guaranteed." It is an estimate of reliability.
  • "Old names." Azure AI Foundry is now Microsoft Foundry; Azure AI Services is now Foundry Tools.

6The final week

Day Do
7–5 One module per day with its card; answer recall questions from memory
4–3 Read the sample programs again line by line; do the pairs and traps out loud
2 Redo all practice questions; list your misses
1 Light review; check the exam time, ID and rules; rest

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Mixed practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors wants its support bot to stay on topic and polite. Where do the rules belong?

  • AIn the project endpoint address
  • BIn the temperature setting
  • CIn the image size parameter
  • DIn the system prompt
Show the answer

Answer: D. The system prompt sets the standing role, scope and tone.

S2Which principle applies when a loan model treats two groups differently for no good reason?

  • ATransparency
  • BFairness
  • CInclusiveness
  • DAccountability
Show the answer

Answer: B. Unequal treatment of groups is a fairness issue.

S3What counts both the prompt and the response against a limit?

  • AThe deployment name
  • BThe context window
  • CThe project endpoint
  • DThe playground
Show the answer

Answer: B. The context window is measured in tokens for prompt plus response.

S4A team needs creative, varied slogans. Which change helps?

  • ALower max tokens to 1
  • BRaise the temperature
  • CSwitch to a speech model
  • DRemove the system prompt
Show the answer

Answer: B. Higher temperature makes answers more varied.

S5An assistant must look up an order and then update a ticket by calling systems. Which approach fits?

  • AAn agent with action tools
  • BKey phrase extraction from tickets
  • CSpeech synthesis of the reply
  • DImage generation for the ticket
Show the answer

Answer: A. Agents use tools to take actions.

S6Which call creates an image from a description?

  • Aresponses.create with an invoice
  • Brecognize_once_async
  • Canalyze_sentiment
  • Dimages.generate
Show the answer

Answer: D. Image generation uses the images.generate call.

S7Which tool extracts fields from invoices and returns a confidence score for each?

  • AAzure Speech for audio
  • BAzure Vision Smart crop
  • CAn embedding model for search
  • DAzure Content Understanding
Show the answer

Answer: D. Content Understanding extracts fields and returns confidence scores.

S8A Python program needs to authenticate to a Foundry project without a key in the code. What does it use?

  • AA password variable in the code
  • BThe deployment name of the model
  • CSSML markup for speech
  • DDefaultAzureCredential
Show the answer

Answer: D. DefaultAzureCredential uses the signed-in Microsoft Entra ID identity.

S9Which speech object states whether audio comes from the microphone or a file?

  • ATextAnalyticsClient
  • BAIProjectClient
  • CAudioConfig
  • DPromptAgentDefinition
Show the answer

Answer: C. AudioConfig defines the audio source.

S10Which deployment type should most workloads start with?

  • ADeveloper tier
  • BGlobal Standard
  • CRegional Provisioned
  • DGlobal Batch
Show the answer

Answer: B. The documentation advises starting with Global Standard.

7.2 Recall questions

R1Name the six responsible AI principles.

Show the answer

Fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency, accountability.

R2What are the three parts of an agent?

Show the answer

Model, instructions and tools.

R3Which method creates an agent version?

Show the answer

project.agents.create_version.

R4What does begin_analyze return?

Show the answer

A poller; call result() to get the analysis.

R5Which exam replaced AI-900?

Show the answer

AI-901.

R6What do you read first in a question?

Show the answer

The last sentence.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Exam AI-901; pass at 700; concepts 40–45%, Foundry implementation 55–60%; AI-900 retired
Method last sentence, key need, name the workload or feature, most specific match; code: client, credential, call, input, output
Biggest confusions system vs user; generative vs agentic; extract vs classify vs generate; analyze vs generate images; standard vs provisioned vs batch
Traps no memory, temperature is variety not accuracy, tokens are not words, reasoning models ignore temperature, old product names
